context.title: Santiago's new hobby
context.text:
Santiago is sixteen and lives in a small town near Manizales. Last year his uncle gave him an old pair of binoculars for his birthday. At first, Santiago didn't know what to do with them. Then one morning he saw a bright green bird in the garden and wanted to know its name. He looked for it in a book at the town library and found out it was a parrot that lives only in the Andes.

Now Santiago gets up at five every Saturday and walks to the forest with two friends from school. They write down every bird they see in a notebook and take photos with a mobile phone. So far they have seen more than ninety different species. Santiago says the hardest part is being quiet for a long time. Next year he wants to study biology at university.

stem: How did Santiago get his binoculars?

options.label: A
options.text: He bought them at the library.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Mezcla dos datos del texto (binoculares y biblioteca).
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. En la biblioteca buscó el nombre del pájaro; no compró nada allí.

options.label: B
options.text: A friend from school lent them.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Asocia a los amigos del colegio con los binoculares.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Los amigos lo acompañan al bosque, pero los binoculares fueron de su tío.

options.label: C
options.text: He found them in the garden.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. En el jardín vio el pájaro verde, no encontró los binoculares.

options.label: D
options.text: They were a present from his uncle.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. El texto dice que su tío se los regaló de cumpleaños («his uncle gave him… for his birthday»).

context.title: The school garden
context.text:
Two years ago, the students at Colegio La Esperanza had an idea. Behind the school there was a piece of land full of rubbish. The students asked the head teacher if they could clean it and use it to grow vegetables. She agreed, but only if they promised to look after it during the holidays too.

Today the garden has tomatoes, lettuce, beans and herbs. Each class is responsible for one part of the garden for a month. The vegetables are used in the school kitchen, and the students eat them at lunch. Last month they grew so many tomatoes that they sold some to families in the neighbourhood and used the money to buy new tools.

The science teacher, Mr Rojas, also uses the garden for his classes. "It's easier to understand how plants grow when you see it with your own eyes," he says.

stem: What was behind the school before the garden?

options.label: A
options.text: A football field for students.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. No era una cancha: era un terreno con basura.

options.label: B
options.text: A small farm with animals.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Imagina un uso anterior que el texto no menciona.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El texto no habla de una granja ni de animales.

options.label: C
options.text: A piece of land with a lot of rubbish.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. El texto dice que era un terreno «full of rubbish» (lleno de basura).

options.label: D
options.text: An old school kitchen.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Confunde la cocina actual con el terreno.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. La cocina se menciona como destino de las verduras, no como lo que había detrás.

context.title: An email from Bogotá
context.text:
Hi Tom,
I've been in Bogotá for three weeks now and I'm really enjoying it. My host family is great. Doña Marta cooks amazing food, and her son Felipe is teaching me to play tejo. It's a traditional game where you throw a heavy metal disc at a target. I'm terrible at it, but it's a lot of fun!

The weather is not what I expected. I thought Colombia was always hot, but Bogotá is high in the mountains, so it's often cold and it rains almost every afternoon. I had to buy a warm jacket in my first week.

My Spanish is getting better. At first I only understood a few words, but now I can have short conversations. My classes at the language school finish next month, and then I'm going to travel to the coast for a week before I go home.

See you soon,
Emma

stem: Who is teaching Emma to play tejo?

options.label: A
options.text: Her friend Tom.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Confunde al destinatario con un personaje del relato.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Tom es a quien le escribe el correo; no está en Bogotá.

options.label: B
options.text: Her host family's son.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. Felipe, el hijo de su familia anfitriona, le está enseñando.

options.label: C
options.text: Doña Marta, the mother.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Confunde a los dos miembros de la familia.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Doña Marta cocina; quien enseña tejo es su hijo.

options.label: D
options.text: Her teacher at the school.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Asocia «teaching» con la escuela de idiomas.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. En la escuela estudia español; el tejo se lo enseña Felipe.

subject: IN

context.title: A young chef
context.text:
Mariana Ortiz is only seventeen, but she already has her own cooking channel on the internet with more than fifty thousand followers. She started cooking when she was eight, helping her grandmother prepare arepas for the family's small restaurant in Barranquilla.

In her videos, Mariana prepares traditional Colombian dishes, but she often changes the recipes to make them healthier. For example, she bakes her empanadas instead of frying them. "I want young people to know that healthy food can also be delicious," she says.

Mariana records her videos on Sunday afternoons, when the restaurant is closed. Her younger brother holds the camera. She doesn't earn much money from the channel yet, but she has received invitations to cook at food festivals. After finishing school, she hopes to study at a cooking school in Lima.

stem: How did Mariana learn to cook?

options.label: A
options.text: At a cooking school in Lima.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Toma un plan futuro como pasado.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Estudiar en Lima es lo que espera hacer después del colegio.

options.label: B
options.text: At a food festival in Barranquilla.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Los festivales son invitaciones recientes, no donde aprendió.

options.label: C
options.text: By helping her grandmother as a child.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. Empezó a los ocho años ayudando a su abuela con las arepas.

options.label: D
options.text: By watching videos on the internet.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Invierte la relación: ella hace videos.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Ella hace videos; no dice que aprendiera viéndolos.

context.title: A young chef
context.text:
Mariana Ortiz is only seventeen, but she already has her own cooking channel on the internet with more than fifty thousand followers. She started cooking when she was eight, helping her grandmother prepare arepas for the family's small restaurant in Barranquilla.

In her videos, Mariana prepares traditional Colombian dishes, but she often changes the recipes to make them healthier. For example, she bakes her empanadas instead of frying them. "I want young people to know that healthy food can also be delicious," she says.

Mariana records her videos on Sunday afternoons, when the restaurant is closed. Her younger brother holds the camera. She doesn't earn much money from the channel yet, but she has received invitations to cook at food festivals. After finishing school, she hopes to study at a cooking school in Lima.

stem: Why does Mariana record on Sunday afternoons?

options.label: A
options.text: The light is better in the afternoon.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El texto no menciona la luz.

options.label: B
options.text: The restaurant is closed then.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. Graba los domingos en la tarde porque el restaurante está cerrado.

options.label: C
options.text: Her followers watch more on Sundays.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Inventa una razón sobre la audiencia.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El texto no habla de cuándo ven los videos sus seguidores.

options.label: D
options.text: Her brother has no school then.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Supone una razón relacionada con el hermano.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El hermano sostiene la cámara, pero la razón dada es el cierre del restaurante.

context.title: My trip to the Tatacoa Desert
context.text:
Last December, my family and I spent three days in the Tatacoa Desert, in Huila. I was surprised because I didn't know Colombia had a desert. It isn't a desert of sand like in films. The ground is red and grey, and there are many cactus plants.

During the day it was very hot, so we stayed in our cabin and only went out early in the morning and late in the afternoon. My favourite part was the night. Because there are no big cities near the desert, the sky is very dark and you can see thousands of stars. We visited a small observatory where a guide showed us Saturn through a telescope. I could see its rings!

If you go, take a hat, a lot of water and sun cream. And don't forget a jacket: the nights can be cooler than you think.

stem: Why was the writer surprised?

options.label: A
options.text: It rained every day of the trip.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El texto dice que hacía mucho calor de día.

options.label: B
options.text: There were no plants in the desert.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. Menciona muchos cactus.

options.label: C
options.text: The desert was full of sand.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El texto dice que no es un desierto de arena.

options.label: D
options.text: The writer didn't know Colombia had a desert.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. Dice «I didn't know Colombia had a desert».

context.title: Phones at the dinner table
context.text:
In many homes, families eat dinner while they look at their phones. A school in Cali wanted to know how this affects family life, so it asked 300 students to answer some questions.

More than half of the students said they use their phones during meals. Many of them said their parents do the same. But when the school asked them to try one week without phones at dinner, the results were interesting. Most students said they talked more with their families and learned things they didn't know about their parents. Some said the first two days were difficult and a bit boring.

After the experiment, 60% of the families decided to keep a "no phones" rule at least three days a week. "Now my dad tells us stories about when he was young," said one student.

stem: Why did the school ask students questions?

options.label: A
options.text: To choose the best phone for students.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El estudio no compara celulares.

options.label: B
options.text: To learn how phones at meals affect families.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. La escuela quería saber cómo afecta a la vida familiar usar el celular en la cena.

options.label: C
options.text: To find out what students eat at home.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. La comida no es el tema; lo es el uso del celular.

options.label: D
options.text: To ban phones in the school.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El experimento fue en casa, durante la cena.

context.title: Reading Club
context.text:
THE PUBLIC LIBRARY READING CLUB IS BACK!

Are you between 13 and 17 years old? Do you love stories, or do you want to start reading more? Join our free reading club this holiday.

We meet every Wednesday from 3 to 5 p.m. in Room 2, on the first floor. Each week we read a short story or a chapter of a novel and then talk about it. You don't need to buy any books: the library gives you a copy, and you can take it home.

At the end of the holidays, members will write their own short story. The best three stories will be printed in the library's magazine.

To join, come to the information desk with a parent or guardian before 15 June. Places are limited to 20 people.

stem: Who can join the reading club?

options.label: A
options.text: Anyone who works at the library.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El club es para jóvenes de 13 a 17 años.

options.label: B
options.text: Teenagers from 13 to 17.
options.explanation_feedback: Correcta. El aviso es para jóvenes entre 13 y 17 años.

options.label: C
options.text: Only students who read a lot.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Ignora que también invita a quienes quieren empezar.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El aviso invita también a quienes quieren empezar a leer.

options.label: D
options.text: Parents and their children.
options.distractor_diagnosis: Confunde el requisito de inscripción con los miembros.
options.explanation_feedback: Incorrecta. El acudiente acompaña la inscripción, pero el club es para jóvenes.
